title: U.S. House · Virginia's 11th District
area: Most of Fairfax County, Virginia, including the City of Fairfax and the towns of Vienna and Herndon.

context.text: This seat became vacant after Rep. Gerald E. "Gerry" Connolly (D) died on May 21, 2025; James Walkinshaw won the September 9, 2025 special election to fill the remainder of Connolly's term with 75.1% of the vote. Connolly had entered the 2026 Democratic primary before withdrawing (he is listed among the withdrawn candidates); Walkinshaw then advanced unopposed in the 2026 primary after other contenders (Stella Pekarsky, Amy Roma and Bree Fram) also withdrew. Arthur Purves advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after it was canceled. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate the race Solid/Safe Democratic as of September 22, 2026.

candidates.name: James Walkinshaw
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after other candidates withdrew and the primary was canceled.

summary.text: James Walkinshaw is the Democratic incumbent seeking his first full term representing Virginia's 11th District, having won a 2025 special election after Rep. Gerry Connolly's death. He serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and the Committee on Homeland Security, focusing on the federal workforce and government operations.

background.text: Represents a district that includes most of Fairfax County, the City of Fairfax, and the towns of Vienna and Herndon.

priorities.text: Protecting the nonpartisan civil service and supporting fair pay, benefits and treatment for federal employees.
Strengthening oversight of federal procurement and information technology and holding the administration accountable.

positions.summary: His official issues page calls access to comprehensive reproductive health care, including abortion, a fundamental right and says he supports federal legislation to safeguard abortion rights nationwide.
positions.quote: access to comprehensive reproductive health care—including contraception, IVF, abortion, prenatal care, and cancer screenings—is a fundamental right

positions.summary: His official issues page says he supports legislation to ban assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, close the Charleston loophole and require background checks on all gun sales.
positions.quote: he supports legislation to ban assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, close the Charleston loophole, require background checks on all gun sales

positions.summary: His official issues page says he is pushing Congress to restore the lapsed Affordable Care Act subsidies and has stood against Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: James has stood firmly against cuts to Medicaid, fighting to protect the critical services millions of families depend on, and is pushing Congress to restore Affordable Care Act subsidies that have already lapsed

positions.summary: His official issues page says he supports federal investment in clean energy and is working to repeal rollbacks of clean-energy tax credits.
positions.quote: In Congress, James supports bold federal action to mobilize federal investments in cheap clean energy, climate resilience, and green jobs.

positions.summary: His official issues page says he has opposed additional funding for ICE and CBP until reforms are delivered, and supports a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.
positions.quote: James has repeatedly held the line against additional funding for ICE and CBP until serious reforms are delivered

positions.summary: His official foreign-affairs page says no president should take the country into war without a vote of Congress.
positions.quote: He believes no president should drag the country into another war without a vote of Congress and a credible plan presented to the American people.

positions.summary: His official economy page lists the current tariffs among policies he is fighting because of their effect on Northern Virginia businesses and workers.
positions.quote: tariffs that threaten businesses and workers

positions.summary: His official housing page says he has pushed for zoning and permitting reforms to increase housing supply and supports the Road to Housing Act to cut red tape and modernize environmental reviews.
positions.quote: pushing for zoning and permitting reforms to increase housing supply

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, which oversees the federal workforce, government operations and federal IT management, and on its Military and Foreign Affairs Subcommittee.
Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security.

candidates.name: Arthur Purves
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Arthur Purves is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent James Walkinshaw. A retired computer programmer and longtime president of the Fairfax County Taxpayers Alliance, he is running on reducing chronic-disease-driven medical spending, opposing carbon-emissions regulation, and family self-sufficiency.

background.text: Received a BA, MBA and MS from the University of Pennsylvania; worked 40 years as a computer programmer.
background.quote: I received a BA, MBA, and MS from the University of Pennsylvania. ... I worked for 40 years as a computer programmer.

background.text: Has served as president of the Fairfax County Taxpayers Alliance for 30 years and treasurer of the Fairfax Committee of 100 for ten years.
Member of the League of Women Voters and the Fairfax branch of the NAACP; has taught ESL in Alexandria and at the Tysons-Pimmit Library.

priorities.text: Reducing federal medical spending by addressing diet-driven chronic disease.
priorities.quote: The federal government spends $2.1 trillion on medical care. Ninety percent is spent on the chronic disease epidemic caused by ultra-processed food and the old high-carb food pyramid.

priorities.text: Opposing state and federal carbon-emissions caps, which he says drive up gas prices.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls Virginia's participation in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative a new tax on consumers, says warming is not a crisis, and calls for ending the "war on fossil fuels."
positions.quote: End the war on fossil fuels to reduce gas and food prices.

positions.summary: His campaign site says abortion always takes a life and that it should remain legal only for the rare cases to save the mother's life.
positions.quote: Keep abortion legal for those rare cases but encourage marriage.

positions.summary: His campaign site says school districts should give vouchers to students who leave public schools for private or home schooling.
positions.quote: School districts should give vouchers to students who attend for at least a year and then leave for private or home-schooling.

positions.summary: His campaign site says it is debatable that complex gun laws reduce crime and that such laws turn law-abiding citizens into inadvertent felons.
positions.quote: That complex gun laws reduce crime is debatable.

summary.text: Dianne Blais is the Green Party candidate on the general-election ballot for Virginia's 11th District. Ballotpedia lists no campaign profile, key messages, or campaign finance activity for her.

researchNotes: Ballotpedia has no staff-curated or survey profile for Walkinshaw beyond his name and party, so his priorities/background rely on his official House biography page; no independent campaign website content was retrieved for him. Blais has no public campaign materials found beyond her ballot listing.
